chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from Abd al-Rahman, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Muhrim (person in Ihram) who removes a louse from his body and throws it away; he said: He gives food in its place.

From him, from Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Muhrim should not deliberately remove a louse from his body or from his garment; and if he kills any of them by mistake, he should give food in its place, a handful with his hand.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muhrim who kills a louse?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of Ihram regarding the removal of lice, distinguishing between deliberate action and accidental killing. While the first chain suggests feeding in place of the louse, the second explicitly states that deliberate removal requires expiation, whereas accidental killing incurs a penalty of a handful of food, reflecting the juristic nuance between 'killing' and 'removing' in ritual purity laws.
